lines: In nineteen seventy-five, saving one photo took twenty-three seconds.
In 1975, saving one photo took 23 seconds.

youtube.title: The First Digital Camera Took 23 Seconds Per Photo (Kodak, 1975)
youtube.description:
In December 1975 Kodak engineer Steven Sasson built a handheld digital camera with a 100 × 100 pixel (0.01 MP) sensor. It weighed about 8 lb (3.6 kg), was roughly the size of a toaster, and took 23 seconds to record one image to a cassette tape; playing it back on a TV took another 23 seconds. A Canon EOS R8 has about 24.2 megapixels, roughly 2,400× more pixels. The landscape shown is a simulation, not a photo from the camera.
#photography #history #shorts
